openDecisions.question: Should the 120px row height change per breakpoint? It is currently fixed at every range, so a two-row tile is 248px tall on a phone and on a 2560 display.

rules.statement: The bento grid class exists.
Rows are a fixed 120px, which is what makes a row span mean something.
Packing is dense, so a short tile backfills a hole left by a tall one instead of leaving a gap.
Row spans exist for the mobile range.
Row spans exist for the tablet range.
Row spans exist for the desktop range.
The row height should be a semantic token like every other dimension in the grid, not a literal in the stylesheet.
rules.detail: --s2a-grid-row-height is not in the built token CSS

openDecisions.question: row-span-* utilities exist for all three ranges but only do anything inside a bento grid, where rows have a fixed height. Should they move to the bento contract or stay general?

rules.statement: Column classes only mean anything inside a row; the row is what creates the grid they span.
The mobile range offers a span for every one of its six columns.
The mobile range stops at six. A col-sm-7 would be a span wider than the grid it sits in.
rules.detail: .col-sm-7 is absent, as the contract states

rules.statement: The desktop range offers a span for every one of its twelve columns.
The tablet range offers a span for every one of its twelve columns.
No range offers a thirteenth column.
rules.detail: .col-lg-13 is absent, as the contract states

rules.statement: Explicit column starts exist for the desktop range, so asymmetric layouts need no spacer elements.
Explicit column starts exist for the tablet range.
col-md-* must be declared after col-lg-* inside the 768 range, or the tablet override never wins. Source order is load-bearing here.
rules.detail: Both families sit in the same @media (min-width: 768px) block with col-md-* second; the 1280 block then re-asserts col-lg-*. Confirmed by reading the stylesheet; a cascade check would need a real CSS cascade model.

rules.statement: The gutter between columns is the same 8px Figma's layout guide uses.

openDecisions.question: The caps are computed from a hard-coded 1440 basis rather than from --s2a-grid-max-width. Should they follow the standard container up to 1920 in HD?
Will's hosted demo documents these under a heading reading 'Desktop Constraint Variations (1024px+)', but they carry no media query at all in either stylesheet.
Should .container-6 used on its own be an error? Alone it sets only a cap — no centring, no side margins — so a section that forgets .container silently sits flush left.

rules.statement: The 12-column cap exists and equals 1440.
The 10-column cap is computed from the grid, not typed as a pixel literal.
rules.detail: max-width is computed: calc(((1440px - (11 * var(--s2a-grid-gutter))) / 12) * 10 + (9 * var(--s2a-grid-gutter)))

rules.statement: The 8-column cap is computed from the grid.
rules.detail: max-width is computed: calc(((1440px - (11 * var(--s2a-grid-gutter))) / 12) * 8 + (7 * var(--s2a-grid-gutter)))

rules.statement: The 6-column cap is computed from the grid.
rules.detail: max-width is computed: calc(((1440px - (11 * var(--s2a-grid-gutter))) / 12) * 6 + (5 * var(--s2a-grid-gutter)))

rules.statement: The gutter token the maths depends on ships.

openDecisions.question: Does the fluid container cap at 2560, as both Figma notes state, or stay genuinely uncapped?

rules.statement: The fluid container class exists.
The fluid container is 100% wide with no cap below HD.
It resets the percentage rule to 100% locally, so a nested row does not inherit an 83.4% width it did not ask for.
The fluid container stops growing at 2560px. Beyond that the layout is no longer a layout, it is a stretched one.
rules.detail: .container-fluid has no block in a range beginning at 1441px; nearest is 0px where max-width is 100%

openDecisions.question: Will's demo renames this container-hd-offset and keeps a fixed spacing-lg padding at every breakpoint instead of switching to the percentage rule at 768. Which behaviour is correct?

rules.statement: The container-hd class exists.
The cap is the HD custom property, 1920 — not a literal repeated in two places.
The HD ceiling resolves to 1920px.
Below 768 the side margin is spacing-lg.
From 768 up it switches to the percentage rule and clears its padding.

openDecisions.question: Once the standard container rises to 1920 in HD, is container-hd still a distinct family or does it collapse into this one?

rules.statement: The container class exists.
Below 768 the side margin is the spacing-lg token, 24px — not a percentage and not a literal.
From 768 up the container width is the 83.4% percentage rule.
From 768 up the padding is cleared, because the percentage rule now supplies the margins. Leaving both on is how a container ends up double-indented.
In HD the cap is 1920, matching Figma's default container family.
rules.detail: .container has no block in a range beginning at 1441px; nearest is 1440px where max-width is 1440px

rules.statement: Figma's default container family says 1920 in the HD mode.
Figma's legacy-retire family — the 1440-everywhere behaviour the stylesheet currently implements — is on its way out, by its own name.
The mobile margin token ships.

openDecisions.question: Rename container-hero-offset to container-token-offset, matching Will's demo and Figma's fixed-offset family?

rules.statement: The offset container class exists.
The mobile margin is 24px, from spacing-lg.
The tablet margin is 40px, from spacing-2xl.
The desktop margin is 64px, from spacing-4xl.
In HD the ladder stops and the percentage rule takes over, at the HD boundary of 1441 — not 1440.
rules.detail: .container-hero-offset has no block in a range beginning at 1441px; nearest is 1440px where padding-left is 0

rules.statement: Figma's offset ladder agrees at mobile: 24px.
Figma's offset ladder agrees at tablet: 40px.
Figma's offset ladder agrees at desktop: 64px.
Figma's fixed offset value is spacing-lg at every mode, which is the value Will quotes as 'fixed offset: --spacing-lg'.
Every rung of the ladder is a shipped token.

openDecisions.question: Will's layout page calls the md column range 'optional'; the stylesheet implements col-md-* unconditionally inside the 768 range. Is col-md a required range or an opt-in override?

rules.statement: The mobile range carries no media query — the system is mobile-first, so sm is the base and every other range is an override.
rules.detail: Verified by the absence of any max-width query in the stylesheet; the sm column classes are declared at the top level.

rules.statement: The tablet range begins at 768px.
The desktop range begins at 1280px.
The HD range begins at 1441px, so that 1440 — the width every desktop mockup is drawn at — is unambiguously inside the desktop range.
rules.detail: the stylesheet declares no range beginning at 1441px; nearest is 1440px

rules.statement: The grid stylesheet and the shipped XL token file must begin the HD range at the same pixel. If they disagree, a layout at that exact width gets its columns from one range and its spacing from the other.
rules.detail: dist/packages/tokens/css/dev/tokens.responsive.xl.css begins at 1441px but the grid stylesheet begins this range at 1440px — a layout at 1440px takes its columns from one range and its spacing from the other

rules.statement: The grid stylesheet and the shipped LG token file must begin the desktop range at the same pixel.
The grid stylesheet and the shipped MD token file must begin the tablet range at the same pixel.
The mobile range has 6 columns.
Every range from 768 up has 12 columns.
Figma's mobile grid mode also says 6 columns.
Figma's HD grid mode also says 12 columns.
The gutter is a semantic token, never a literal. 8px typed by hand is how a grid stops being a system.
Figma's layout guide gap resolves to the same 8px as the code gutter, in every mode.
The gutter token ships in the built token CSS.
The mobile side-margin token ships in the built token CSS.
The row primitive exists and is the only thing that establishes a grid context.
A tablet-portrait reflow, when a layout needs one, uses 900px — not a value invented per block. Figma records the same number as viewport._min-width-899 in the tablet mode.

openDecisions.question: What is the canonical object minimum — 230px, as Will's note says covers the mocks, or a token on the spacing scale?
Will's note says an object grid can live inside or outside a container. If outside, what supplies its side margins?
Does the object grid need the orphan behaviour the ups grid has, where a lone last item stretches?

rules.statement: No object-grid class exists in S2A yet. This contract is the specification, and this rule is what keeps that honest.
rules.detail: .object-grid is absent, as the contract states

rules.statement: No object minimum custom property exists yet.
rules.detail: --s2a-object-min is absent, as the contract states

rules.statement: The gutter token the system would use already ships, so the implementation needs no new tokens.
Figma's layout guide confirms the 8px gutter the name refers to.

openDecisions.question: At the tablet breakpoint, section-spacing 3xl resolves to 64px while 2xl resolves to 80px — the scale inverts. Intended or a mapping slip?

Will's cheat sheet names ten spacer roles — Base Top/Bottom, Grid Bottom, Blocks Gap, Cards Bottom, Cards Gap, CTA Top/Bottom, Pothole, Rich Content Bottom — each with four per-breakpoint values. Should those roles become semantic tokens that alias the scale, so a block says 'cta-top' rather than picking a step?

rules.statement: Every step of the section-spacing scale ships in the built token CSS. A gap in the scale is how a block ends up with a literal.
The scale includes an explicit zero, so 'no gap' is a choice from the system rather than the absence of one.
The viewport vertical padding scale ships.
Figma's HD mode agrees that the largest section gap is 240px.
Figma's mobile mode compresses the largest section gap to 80px.
The scale never goes backwards: at every breakpoint each step is greater than or equal to the one below it. Will found 2xl and 3xl inverted in the spacers once already.
rules.detail: Checked by the validator across all four modes; see the conformance report. At md, 3xl (64) is smaller than 2xl (80) — recorded as a finding rather than silently tolerated.

rules.statement: The md token file begins at 768, not 1024. The 1024 value flipped sectional spacing a whole range early and shipped for months.

openDecisions.question: Who implements the ups grid — S2A or C2/Milo?
Is 'always two-up at tablet' right for five-up and six-up sets, or should they go three-up at tablet?

rules.statement: No ups-grid class exists in S2A. The system is fully specified in Figma and implemented nowhere this repository can see.
rules.detail: .ups-grid is absent, as the contract states

rules.statement: No N-up modifier exists in S2A either.
rules.detail: .two-up is absent, as the contract states

rules.statement: The orphan rule exists in no stylesheet here.
rules.detail: .orphan-full is absent, as the contract states

rules.statement: This is block-tier, so S2A must not add shipped tokens for it. Will: 'if its block level rules it wont be in s2a'.
rules.detail: No tokens are declared beyond the shared gutter, which the foundation already ships. Re-check if this contract ever grows a token list of its own.

rules.statement: The shared gutter token exists, so an implementation needs nothing new from the token pipeline.

scaleFindings.detail: section-spacing 2xs (8) is smaller than 3xs (16) at sm
section-spacing 2xl (24) is smaller than xl (40) at sm
section-spacing md (24) is smaller than sm (32) at md
section-spacing 3xl (64) is smaller than 2xl (80) at md
